q: Under the Adjutant General's Open Door Policy, how should Soldiers request an appointment with the TAG?

q: Under MNNG policy, must Soldiers tell their chain of command before filing an IG complaint?
answer: No; they are not required to disclose the IG visit or discuss the issue with their supervisor, First Sergeant, or Commander first

Yes, the First Sergeant must be informed in writing
Only if the complaint involves the chain of command

q: Under the MNNG Military Equal Opportunity Policy, how long do Soldiers have to file an EO complaint?
answer: 180 days from the date of the last alleged harassment or discriminatory action
quote: Soldiers and Airmen have 180 days from the date of the last alleged harassment or discriminatory
why: The MNNG policy allows 180 days, longer than the 60 days in AR 600-20.

q: Under the MNARNG Drug Testing Policy, what percentage of assigned end strength must commanders randomly test each month?
answer: At least 10 percent
quote: Commanders will randomly test at least 10% of their assigned end strength each month.
why: If a month is missed, at least 20 percent must be tested the next month, and never two months in a row.

q: Under the MNNG Substance Abuse Policy, how much prevention education must traditional Army Soldiers complete each year?
answer: A minimum of 2 hours, completed no later than 30 September each year
wrong: 8 hours by the end of annual training

why: Full-time members must complete 4 hours.

q: Under the MNNG Sexual Harassment Policy, where are Soldiers who experience sexual harassment first referred?

quote: Soldiers and Airmen who experience sexual harassment will be first referred to the Sexual Assault Prevention and Response office
why: They are entitled to victim advocate services from SAPR.

q: What is the Minnesota National Guard's stance on harassment in the workplace?
